approval_notes: Orchestrator-directed follow-up to the merged F008 Slice S2 (PR #39, merged as ed2a6c9), raised by the Level-2 evaluator as Observation A and required BEFORE Wave 3 launches, because all six concurrent provider slices sit on this sync path.

THE DEFECT (live-reproduced by the evaluator): in sync_coverage() the 'unknown_category' and 'unknown_source' branches 'continue' WITHOUT adding category_id to declared_category_ids, so the prune loop treats a still-declared pair as no-longer-declared and DELETES its row. Repro: sync Cloudflare -> 14 rows; rename the two referenced source slugs in the DB; re-sync -> {unchanged: 12, unknown_source: 2, withdrawn: 2}, rows 14 -> 12, and serverless-functions + containers-app-hosting regress to undeclared/'unknown' in the public API. Restoring the slugs and re-syncing returns 14.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN IT LOOKS: the silent prune dropped Cloudflare's evidence-backed count from 3 (exactly the Q9-A floor) to 1 with NO hard failure. The Q9-A floor was enforced only as a CONFIG-LOAD invariant, never as a DATABASE invariant, so the catalogue could erode below the floor while every individual surviving row stayed legal.

TIGHT SCOPE, NO MIGRATION. Alembic head stays 0011_provider_category_coverage. Every S2 guardrail still binds: no new runtime or test dependency (Q6-A); no Redis; no live network (Q3-A); no credentialed provider API (Q5-A); no secrets; no FTS; Q11 unchanged (derivation stays computed, never stored); region/residency stay out of scope (Q8-A).

Four further evaluator observations are tracked follow-ups and are explicitly NOT in scope here: (B) staleness masking a genuine free-tier withdrawal (needs an owner product ruling); (C) a (verified_free, unknown) pair staying silent forever; (D) contradiction-reader fragility against new Wave-3 ReviewItem producers; (E) _applied_revisions() asserting the script graph rather than the DB.
objective: Make a declared coverage row survive a reference this sync cannot resolve, and make the Q9-A evidence floor a DATABASE invariant rather than only a config-load one. Concretely: (a) sync_coverage() registers a pair as declared BEFORE any resolution step that can fail, so an unresolvable 'source' (or an unseeded category) is recorded as a resolution FAILURE and leaves the stored row intact, never as a withdrawal that prunes it; (b) after the upsert and the prune, sync_coverage() re-reads the PERSISTED rows for that provider and asserts the same >= MIN_EVIDENCE_BACKED_COVERAGE evidence-backed verified_free/offered_no_z0 floor that validate_coverage_floor() enforces at load, raising CoverageFloorError (a ValueError) on a shortfall so the erosion is rolled back with the caller's transaction and can never commit; and (c) the unknown_category / unknown_source outcomes stay in the returned counts so the condition remains observable to the caller instead of being silently absorbed.
scope: apps/api/app/ingest/config_sync.py: move 'declared_category_ids.add(category_id)' ABOVE the source-resolution step, so neither the unknown_category nor the unknown_source branch can reach the prune loop with the pair unregistered. A failure to resolve a reference is not a withdrawal of the declaration.

apps/api/app/ingest/config_sync.py: new CoverageFloorError(ValueError) and _assert_persisted_coverage_floor(), called at the end of sync_coverage() AFTER the final flush. It re-queries provider_category_coverage for the provider (so it measures the DATABASE, not what the code believes it wrote) and counts rows whose state is in EVIDENCE_BACKED_COVERAGE_STATES and which carry a source_id or an evidence_url -- the same predicate validate_coverage_floor() uses at load. Below MIN_EVIDENCE_BACKED_COVERAGE it raises with the found list, the shortfall and the unresolved references that caused it.

apps/api/app/ingest/config_sync.py: the floor assertion is skipped only when the canonical taxonomy is entirely absent from the database (no category rows matched at all), which is the documented pre-0010 no-op path where sync_coverage writes nothing and there is therefore nothing to erode. Any partially seeded taxonomy is checked.

apps/api/app/ingest/config_sync.py: CoverageDeclarationOutcome for unknown_source now carries the surviving row's coverage_id when one exists, so a caller can see that the declaration was preserved rather than dropped; the withdrawn outcome now carries the real category slug instead of an empty string.

tests/integration/test_ingest_config_sync.py: the evaluator's exact reproduction -- sync Cloudflare to 14 rows, rename the referenced source slugs in the DB, re-sync, and assert the row count stays 14, that the affected categories remain declared with their prior state and source_id, that the outcomes report unknown_source and ZERO withdrawn, and that the public read API still reports them as declared.

tests/integration/test_ingest_config_sync.py: the post-sync floor assertion fires when the persisted rows genuinely fall below the floor, and does not fire on the healthy path or on a repeat idempotent run.

tests/unit/test_config_system.py: the DB-level floor predicate and the config-load floor predicate are pinned to the same constant and the same evidence-backed state set, so the two cannot drift apart.

acceptance_criteria: 1. The evaluator's reproduction no longer regresses: after breaking the two source references in the database and re-syncing, provider_category_coverage still holds 14 rows for Cloudflare, serverless-functions and containers-app-hosting keep their declared state and source_id, and the run reports ZERO withdrawn.
2. The unknown_source (and unknown_category) condition stays observable: the returned CoverageSyncResult still counts it, so the caller can act on it.

3. The Q9-A floor is a database invariant: when the persisted rows for a provider fall below MIN_EVIDENCE_BACKED_COVERAGE evidence-backed verified_free/offered_no_z0 rows, sync_coverage raises CoverageFloorError with an actionable message, so the erosion is rolled back with the caller's transaction and never commits. Silence is not an acceptable outcome.
4. The healthy path is unaffected: a first sync, an idempotent re-sync and a legitimate state change all still succeed, and a re-run against a byte-identical config still reports zero changes.

risks: Raising on a floor shortfall aborts the caller's transaction, which is a deliberately louder failure mode than the previous silence. Mitigated by scoping the check to the provider being synced, by skipping it entirely on the documented pre-0010 no-op path where nothing is written, and by an actionable message naming the unresolved references. A pending review_item was rejected as the failure mode because it would record the erosion only AFTER committing it -- precisely the silent-degradation bug being fixed.

Wave 3 slices could trip the new raise if they onboard a provider against a partially-synced database. That is the intended behaviour: it is exactly the condition that silently eroded Cloudflare, and it now fails attributably at sync time instead of surfacing later as missing catalogue coverage.

The floor predicate is duplicated between config load and post-sync. Mitigated by sharing MIN_EVIDENCE_BACKED_COVERAGE and EVIDENCE_BACKED_COVERAGE_STATES and by a drift test pinning the two to the same constants.
